Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which numbers are added can affect the result due to rounding errors. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate sums, which, when rounded at each step, yield distinct final results. The presence of finite precision in floating-point representation exacerbates these discrepancies, leading to non-associativity.

Floating-point addition is not associative because the order of operations can affect the rounding errors introduced at each step. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate results due to these rounding errors. Consequently, \((a + b) + c\) may not equal \(a + (b + c)\) in floating-point arithmetic.
